meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, little one!

examples.text: Хочу немножко привести себя в порядок.
examples.trans: I want to get myself in shape a bit.
Hello, Iosif! Sorry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'sorry', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, chef.

examples.text: Костян, извини. Я обещал Вике не врать.
examples.trans: Kostyan, sorry. I promised Vika not to lie.
Hello, Iosif! Sorry.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты опять намекаешь, что я толстый?
examples.trans: Are you hinting again that I am fat?

examples.text: Нет, я просто говорю, что был стройный.
examples.trans: No, I am just saying that you were slim.
What is the matter, Lyova? Easy.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, that is what it is.
It is just a crack!

examples.text: Я изменился, я сейчас это докажу.
examples.trans: I have changed, I will prove it right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Good morning.
You have an incomplete rib fracture.
Well, that is what it is.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have to tell me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You said it was a crack.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I just wanted to check.
I just wanted to check!
I wanted to pull a prank, guys.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be'.

examples.trans: I wanted to look like you.
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'хожий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('similar, looking like').

examples.trans: You look like Iosif Prigozhin.
Well done, he looks like him! Congratulations.
Then he would have looked completely alike.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Be glad. How was the injury sustained?
I would rather have some water.
You would have done better to grow it here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Be glad. How was the injury sustained?

Listen, how slim you used to be!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты что, не видел, что я здесь стою?
examples.trans: Did you not see that I am standing here?
I am simply tidying up here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'растить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'grew out'.

examples.trans: You would have done better to grow it here.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и отрастить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and grew out on time.

examples.trans: Go have breakfast later.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лава'). Common feminine noun meaning 'glory' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And thank goodness!
No, thank God.

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'to God' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And thank goodness!
Thank God!
No, thank God.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It is even heavier than that.

examples.text: Да я могу похудеть в любой момент!
examples.trans: I can lose weight at any moment!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Пять минут, и никуда не уходи, ладно?
examples.trans: Five minutes, and do not go anywhere, okay?

examples.text: Ладно, пачкай тарелки, потом иди мой.
examples.trans: Alright, dirty the plates, then go wash them.
No way!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: That is outrageous! Lyova, forgive me, please.
Forgive me, I mixed everything up.
Forgive me for not believing you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have an incomplete rib fracture.
No. Stop it!
And why do I not know?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'believed', paired with 'верить'.

examples.text: То есть Пригожину ты поверишь, а мне нет?
examples.trans: So you will believe Prigozhin, and not me?

examples.text: Вика, подожди! Не отпущу, пока не поверишь.
examples.trans: Vika, wait! I will not let you go until you believe me.
Forgive me for not believing you.
